paragraphs: References in this Annual Report on Form 10-K to "Interface," "the Company," "we," "our," "ours" and "us" refer to Interface, Inc. and its subsidiaries or any of them, unless the context requires otherwise.

Interface, Inc. was incorporated in Georgia in 1973 and is a global flooring solutions company offering an integrated portfolio of flooring products to customers, including carpet tile, luxury vinyl tile ("LVT"), nora® rubber flooring, and FLOR® premium area rugs. We are a global sustainability leader and offer an extensive range of low carbon and cradle-to-gate carbon negative products that prioritize our sustainability goals.

Over the past decade, we have evolved from a company focused primarily on modular carpet into an integrated flooring solutions provider. In late 2016, we began offering LVT products in select markets, expanding globally in 2017 to capitalize on the high-growth resilient flooring market. In 2018, we acquired nora systems GmbH, adding rubber flooring to our portfolio and strengthening our position in healthcare, education, and transportation market segments. In 2020, we launched our CQuest™ carbon negative carpet tile backings, and in 2021 we set carbon reduction targets validated by the Science Based Targets Initiative. We have also implemented our One Interface strategy, a multi-year organizational initiative that positions us to operate as one global team across our integrated product portfolio. These developments have helped us to diversify beyond our traditional corporate office market segment, building a more resilient revenue base across education, healthcare, government, hospitality, and other commercial end-markets.

As a global company with a reputation for high quality, reliability and premium positioning, we market our integrated portfolio for carpet tile under the established brand names Interface® and FLOR®, we market LVT under the brand Interface®, and we market rubber flooring under the brands noraplan® and norament®.

The Company has two operating and reportable segments – namely Americas ("AMS") and Europe, Africa, Asia and Australia (collectively "EAAA"). The AMS operating segment includes the United States, Canada and Latin America geographic areas. See Note 19 entitled "Segment Information" included in Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for additional information.
Below is a summary of total net sales percentages by reportable segment for the last three fiscal years.

Our business, as well as the commercial interiors industry in general, is cyclical in nature and is impacted by economic conditions and trends that affect the markets for commercial and institutional business spaces. We believe the appeal and utilization of our products will continue to grow, and we are using our considerable skills and experience with designing, producing and marketing our products to make us a market leader. We primarily focus our sales efforts on the corporate office, education, healthcare, public buildings, retail, transportation, and residential living market segments.

Disruptions in global economic markets due to the impact of government-imposed tariffs and retaliatory tariffs, supply chain challenges and disruptions, significant pressures in the commercial office market globally, inflation, slow market conditions in certain parts of the globe, and geopolitical factors including wars and other conflicts, all pose challenges for us and impact the markets we operate in.
Our AMS and EAAA reportable segments sell the same products within their respective geographical regions.

Our modular carpet systems are marketed under the established brands Interface and FLOR. We manufacture carpet tile in precise, dimensionally stable squares - usually 50 cm x 50 cm tiles as well as planks in varying sizes. Carpet tile is produced in a variety of colors, patterns, textures, pile heights, and densities. These options are designed to meet the practical and aesthetic needs of a broad spectrum of commercial interiors — particularly offices, educational facilities, healthcare facilities, government-related facilities (including but not limited to airports), retail spaces, hospitality spaces, and residential interiors. We make carpet tile with yarn containing varying degrees of recycled post-consumer nylon, depending on the style and color. We also make carpet tile backing containing post-industrial and/or post-consumer recycled materials. While we continue to manufacture and sell a substantial portion of our carpet tile in standard styles, most of our modular carpet sales in the Americas and Asia-Pacific regions are made-to-order products designed to meet customer specifications.
We design our carpet tile backing options for dimensional stability. Our two primary backing platforms are:
•GlasBac® - this backing includes a fiberglass-reinforced polymeric composite that reduces the need for adhesives or fasteners.
•CQuest™ backings include bio-based materials and recycled content. When measured on a stand-alone basis, the backings are net carbon negative (see discussion below for additional information).

headings: Risk Factors Related to our Business and Operations
Our earnings could be adversely affected by non-cash adjustments to goodwill, when a test of goodwill assets indicates a material impairment of those assets.
Changes in foreign trade policies and tariffs may adversely impact our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
Large increases in the cost of our raw materials, shipping costs, duties or tariffs could adversely affect us if we are unable to offset them or pass these cost increases through to our customers.
The market price of our common stock has been volatile and the value of your investment may decline.
Sales of our principal products have been and may continue to be affected by adverse economic conditions and cycles, and effects in the new construction market and renovation market.
Disruptions to or failures of information technology systems we use could adversely affect our business.

The impact of potential changes to environmental laws and regulations and industry standards regarding climate change and other sustainability matters could lead to unforeseen disruptions to our business operations.
The conflicts between Russia and Ukraine and in the Middle East could adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial position.
Fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates have had, and could continue to have, an adverse impact on our financial condition and results of operations.
Risk Factors Related to our Indebtedness
We have a substantial amount of debt, which could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations and our ability to meet our payment obligations under our debt.
Servicing our debt requires a significant amount of cash, and we may not have sufficient cash flow from our operations to pay our indebtedness.
We may incur substantial additional indebtedness, which could further exacerbate the risks associated with our substantial indebtedness.
We face risks associated with litigation and claims.

Any or all of the following risk factors could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects.

We compete with a large number of manufacturers in the highly competitive floorcovering products market, and some of these competitors have greater financial resources than we do. We may face challenges competing on price, making investments in our business, or competing on product design or sustainability.

The floorcovering industry is highly competitive. Globally, we compete for sales of floorcovering products with other carpet manufacturers and manufacturers of other types of floorcovering. Although the industry has experienced significant consolidation, a large number of manufacturers remain in the industry. From time to time, our competitors add or modify manufacturing capacity throughout the globe, which increases the amount or cost structure of supply in the market. Increased capacity or manufacturing efficiencies at our competitors could result in pricing pressure on our products and less demand for our products, thus adversely affecting both revenues and profitability.

Some of our competitors, including a number of large diversified domestic and foreign companies who manufacture modular carpet and resilient flooring as one segment of their business, have greater financial resources than we do. Competing effectively may require us to make additional investments in our product development efforts, manufacturing facilities, distribution network, and sales and marketing activities.

In addition, we often compete on design preferences. Our customers' design preferences may evolve or change before we adapt quickly enough to those changes or before we recognize those changes have happened in the marketplace. If this occurs, it could negatively affect our sales as our customers choose other product offerings that more closely align with their design preferences. Moreover, as our competitors improve the sustainability attributes of their products and operations, or if our competitors market the sustainability attributes of their products or operations more effectively than we do, it could negatively affect the degree to which we differentiate from our competitors on those attributes which could negatively affect our ability to compete and gain those sales as customers choose product offerings from our competitors instead of our product offerings. In situations such as these, we may be required by accounting rules to recognize a loss for the write-down of the value of our inventory due to its age or obsolescence.

We undertake an annual review of the goodwill asset balance reflected in our financial statements. Our review is conducted during the fourth quarter of the year, unless there has been a triggering event prescribed by applicable accounting rules that warrants an earlier interim testing for possible goodwill impairment. A future goodwill impairment test may result in a future non-cash adjustment, which could adversely affect our earnings for any such future period.

paragraphs: Our One Interface strategy continues to fuel growth as we strengthen global capabilities, improve commercial productivity, and simplify and optimize our operations. During 2025, we had consolidated net sales of $1,386.9 million, up 5.4% compared to $1,315.7 million in 2024, primarily due to higher customer demand — particularly in the healthcare and education market segments. Consolidated operating income for 2025 was $164.0 million compared to consolidated operating income of $134.4 million in 2024, primarily due to higher sales and higher gross profit margin driven by higher average sales prices, favorable product mix, and manufacturing efficiencies, partially offset by higher input costs and tariff costs. Consolidated net income for 2025 was $116.1 million, or $1.96 per diluted share, compared to consolidated net income of $86.9 million, or $1.48 per diluted share, in 2024.

During 2024, we had consolidated net sales of $1,315.7 million, up 4.3% compared to $1,261.5 million in 2023, primarily due to increased customer demand – particularly in the retail and education market segments. Consolidated operating income for 2024 was $134.4 million compared to consolidated operating income of $104.5 million in 2023, primarily due to higher sales volumes and lower raw material costs. Consolidated net income for 2024 was $86.9 million, or $1.48 per diluted share, compared to consolidated net income of $44.5 million, or $0.76 per diluted share, in 2023.
A detailed discussion of our 2025 and 2024 consolidated and segment performance appears below under "Analysis of Results of Operations".

paragraphs: 本年度報告書（Form 10-K）中提及 "Interface"、"the Company"、"we"、"our"、"ours" 及 "us"，均指 Interface, Inc. 及其子公司或其中之一，除非文意另有要求。
Interface, Inc. 於 1973 年在喬治亞州成立，為一家全球地板解決方案公司，提供整合型地板產品組合給客戶，包括模組化地毯、奢華乙烯基地板（"LVT"）、nora® 橡膠地板及 FLOR® 高端地毯。我們為全球永續發展領導者，提供廣泛的低碳及從源頭到門口（cradle-to-gate）負碳產品，以落實我們的永續發展目標。

過去十年，我們已從一家主要專注於模組化地毯的公司，進化為整合型地板解決方案供應商。2016 年末，我們開始在部分市場提供 LVT 產品，並於 2017 年 globally 擴張，以抓住高成長的彈性地板市場。2018 年，我們收購 nora systems GmbH，將橡膠地板加入產品組合，並強化在醫療、教育及運輸市場的佔有率。2020 年，我們推出 CQuest™ 負碳地毯地磚背板，2021 年我們設定了經科學基準目標倡議（Science Based Targets Initiative）認證的碳減排目標。我們也實施了 One Interface 策略，為一項多年期的組織倡議，使我們能以一隻全球團隊運作於我們的整合型產品組合。這些發展有助於我們超越傳統企業辦公室市場，建立更穩健的收入基礎，涵蓋教育、醫療、政府、旅館及其他商業終端市場。
作為一家以高品質、可靠性和高定位聞名的全球公司，我們以 Interface® 和 FLOR® 品牌行銷我們的整合型地毯地磚產品組合，以 Interface® 品牌行銷 LVT 產品，並以 noraplan® 和 norament® 品牌行銷橡膠地板。
本公司有兩個營運及應報告分部，即美洲（"AMS"）及歐洲、非洲、亞洲及澳洲（合稱 "EAAA"）。AMS 營運分部包括美國、加拿大及拉丁美洲地理區域。請參閱本年度報告書（Form 10-K）第 8 項中標題為 "分部資訊" 的附註 19，以取得更多資訊。
以下為過去三個會計年度各應報告分部總淨銷售額百分比的總結。
我們的業務，以及整體商業內裝行業，具有週期性特質，並受總體經濟條件及趨勢影響，這些條件及趨勢會影響商業及機構空間的市場。我們認為我們產品的吸引力及使用率將持續成長，我們正運用我們在設計、製造及行銷產品方面的豐富經驗與技能，使我們成為市場領導者。我們主要將銷售努力集中在企業辦公室、教育、醫療、公共建築、零售、運輸及住宅生活市場分部。
全球經濟市場因政府課徵關稅及報復性關稅、供應鏈挑戰與中斷、全球商業辦公室市場的重大壓力、通貨膨脹、某些地區市場成長遲緩，以及地緣政治因素包括戰爭及其他衝突，皆對我們造成挑戰，並影響我們所經營的市場。
我們的 AMS 與 EAAA 應報告分部在其各自地理區域內銷售相同產品。

我們的模組化地毯系統以 Interface 與 FLOR 這兩個已建立的品牌進行行銷。我們製造的地毯地磚為精確且尺寸穩定的正方形 - 通常為 50 公分 x 50 公分的地磚，以及不同尺寸的木板。地毯地磚有各種顏色、圖案、質感、纖維高度與密度選擇。這些選擇是為了滿足廣泛商業空間的實用與美觀需求，特別是辦公室、教育設施、醫療設施、政府相關設施（包括但不限於機場）、零售空間、旅館空間與住宅空間。我們製造的地毯地磚包含不同程度的回收後消費者尼龍纖維，視風格與顏色而定。我們也製造包含後工業與/或後消費者回收材料的地毯地磚背層。雖然我們持續製造與銷售大量標準風格的地毯地磚，但我們在美洲與亞太地區的大多數模組化地毯銷售為訂製產品，以符合客戶的特定需求。
我們設計地毯地磚背層選項以確保尺寸穩定性。我們的兩種主要背層平台為：
•GlasBac® - 這種背層包含纖維增強聚合物複合材料，可減少對黏合劑或固定件的依賴。
•CQuest™ 背層包含生物基材料與回收內容。若單獨測量，這些背層為淨碳負排放（請參閱下方討論以取得更多資訊）。

paragraphs: 本公司 One Interface 策略持續推動成長，因我們強化全球能力、提升商業生產力，並簡化與優化營運。2025 年，本公司合併淨銷售額為 1,386.9 百萬美元，較 2024 年的 1,315.7 百萬美元成長 5.4%，主要因客戶需求增加 — 尤其在醫療與教育市場區段。2025 年本公司合併營運收入為 164.0 百萬美元，較 2024 年的 134.4 百萬美元成長，主要因銷售增加與毛利率提高，由平均銷售價格提高、產品組合改善與製造效率提升所驅動，部分抵銷因輸入成本與關稅成本增加的影響。2025 年本公司合併淨收入為 116.1 百萬美元，或每股稀釋後收益 1.96 美元，較 2024 年的 86.9 百萬美元，或每股稀釋後收益 1.48 美元為高。

2024 年，本公司合併淨銷售額為 1,315.7 百萬美元，較 2023 年的 1,261.5 百萬美元成長 4.3%，主要因客戶需求增加 — 尤其在零售與教育市場區段。2024 年本公司合併營運收入為 134.4 百萬美元，較 2023 年的 104.5 百萬美元成長，主要因銷售量增加與原物料成本降低。2024 年本公司合併淨收入為 86.9 百萬美元，或每股稀釋後收益 1.48 美元，較 2023 年的 44.5 百萬美元，或每股稀釋後收益 0.76 美元為高。
本公司 2025 年及 2024 年合併與各應報告分部之營運表現詳細討論，請參閱後述 "營運成果分析" 部分。

paragraphs: 您在決定是否買進或賣出本公司證券前，應仔細考慮下列因素，並配合本年度10-K表報表及其他文件所包含之資訊，以及本文件所引用之其他文件資訊。任何或全部下列風險因素，均可能對本公司之業務、財務狀況、營運成果與前景造成重大不利影響。
本公司在高度競爭的地板覆蓋產品市場中，與許多製造商競爭，其中一些競爭對手擁有比本公司更龐大的財務資源。本公司可能在價格競爭、對業務進行投資，或在產品設計或永續性方面面臨挑戰。
地板覆蓋產業競爭激烈。全球範圍內，本公司與其他地毯製造商及其他類型地板覆蓋製造商競爭銷售地板覆蓋產品。雖然該產業已歷經顯著的併購，但產業內仍存在大量製造商。不時地，我們的競爭對手會在全球範圍內增加或調整製造能力，這會增加市場的供應量或成本結構。我們競爭對手的製造能力增加或製造效率提升，可能導致我們產品的價格壓力，並降低對我們產品的需求，進而對營收與獲利造成不利影響。
部分競爭對手，包括一些大型多元化國內外公司，他們將模組化地毯與彈性地板製造作為其業務的一個部門，擁有比本公司更龐大的財務資源。有效競爭可能需要本公司在產品開發、製造設施、配送網路與銷售與行銷活動上進行額外投資。

此外，我們經常在設計偏好上進行競爭。我們客戶的設計偏好可能在我們適應這些變化或察覺這些變化已發生在市場之前就已經改變。如果發生這種情況，可能會對我們的銷售造成負面影響，因為客戶可能選擇其他更符合其設計偏好的產品。此外，當我們的競爭對手改善其產品或運營的永續性特徵，或當他們比我們更有效地行銷其產品或運營的永續性特徵時，可能會對我們在這些特徵上的差異化程度造成負面影響，進而影響我們的競爭能力與獲取這些銷售的機會，因為客戶可能選擇競爭對手的產品而非我們的產品。在這些情況下，根據會計規則，我們可能需要承認因存貨過時或淘汰而減值所導致的損失。
本公司每年會對財務報表中所反映的商譽資產餘額進行審查。此審查於每年第四季進行，除非根據適用的會計規則，已發生觸發事件，需要進行較早的中期測試以評估可能的商譽減損。未來的商譽減損測試可能會導致未來的非現金調整，這可能會對任何未來期間的營收造成不利影響。
